title: Vanishing Point (CBC)
paragraphs: CBC's imaginative anthology moves between science fiction, horror, psychological drama, mystery, and fantasy, using both original plays and literary adaptations to explore the border between reality and the strange.

CBC speculative-drama anthology created and produced by Bill Lane and hosted by David Calderisi. The regular first two seasons mixed original Canadian radio plays with adaptations across science fiction, horror, thriller, psychological drama and other speculative forms. The frozen GRH set contains 24 selected broadcasts from historical episode #1 through #69, not a contiguous run.

GRH documents the program through First regular anthology season (October 5, 1984 to May 24, 1985) on [[org|org.vp.4ad028d3bc03e0f3|CBC Radio]] and Second regular anthology season (September 30, 1985 to June 30, 1986) on [[org|org.vp.4ad028d3bc03e0f3|CBC Radio]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Steve Petch (writer on 2 recordings and radio adaptor on 1 recording), Tim Wynne-Jones (radio adaptor on 1 recording and writer on 1 recording), Alberto Manguel (radio adaptor on 1 recording), Alfred Silver (writer on 1 recording), Arthur Samuels (radio adaptor on 1 recording), Carol Bolt (writer on 1 recording), and Christina Meeker (writer on 1 recording).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include speculative fiction and altered reality, psychological disturbance and perception, original Canadian radio drama, literary adaptation for radio, science fiction and future technology, and horror, uncanny and supernatural experience.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Open Wide binaural experiment, CBC launches Vanishing Point as Nightfall follow-up, First regular anthology season, and Second regular anthology season.
